newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury 6 pct 10-yr seen MBS mart's 3rd rail.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury 6 pct 10-yr seen MBS mart's 3rd rail.

text.p: Discount mortgage-backed securities (MBS) coupons were up 1/32 to 3/32 late Wednesday, while 8-1/2 percent coupons were off by 1/32 to 2/32.
One buysider saw continued down-in-coupon trading and participants agreed that further declines in Treasury rates were a source of concern for MBS investors.
"A 6.0-percent yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note is the third rail for the mortgage market," the investor said.
MBS spreads continued to widen as the market lagged slightly behind Treasuries, participants said.

Within the mortgage market itself, "Coupons have compressed considerably," with discounts outperforming high coupons amid prepayment worries, said a New York-based Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA) trader.
Market players reported that there was some paring of positions in 7.0-percent and 7-1/2 percent MBS paper, which had recently grown more expensive due to down-in-coupon trades.
Meanwhile, a New York pass-through trader said "There is a good REMIC (real estate mortgage investment conduit) bid in the market which is taking collateral out of the market."

While the GNMA trader saw some mortgage banker selling, another trader said that it would take another three to four basis point-widening in spreads before mortgage bankers sell MBS. "We haven't really traded off enough to see mortgage bankers sell bonds," he said.

Another market player noted that there was activity in the so-called dollar roll market for conventional mortgage loan-backed MBS. Those are loans originated by banks or thrifts that are based solely on real estate as security and are not insured by a government agency.

"A lot of customers are rolling up positions," he said, explaining that dollar rolls are an alternative to repurchase agreements (repos). MBS participants use the dollar roll market to fund pass-through positions at levels which can be less expensive than the repo market. The objective is to meet deliveries in the broker market.

Separately, MBS participants were bracing for the June Producer Price Index (PPI) report which is due early Friday. The overall PPI index was expected to be unchanged, while PPI without food and energy was predicted to have risen 0.1 percent, a Reuters survey of economists found.

Among key MBS issues, GNMA 7-1/2 percent 30-year bonds advanced 2/32 to 101-11/32 bid to a bond equivalent yield of 7.33 percent. Comparable Federal National Mortgage Association securities declined 1/32 to 101-03/32 while Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. securities also fell 1/32, to 101-08/32.

Ten-year Treasury notes rose 3/32 to 102-22/32 to yield 6.25 percent and the 30-year Treasury bond gained 7/32 to 100-25/32 for a 6.56 percent yield. ((-- Lynn Adler, 212-859-1677, & Aleksandrs Rozens,
